name: vx6-preclass-single-classification-reuse-d1-d4-20270520-20270526
qualityPolicyNotes: Serial 52 (Checklist B) implements 24.23.2 single-classification reuse on top of A/51: wc_preclass_classify_query stops double-scanning the generated table by reusing the already-found row through the new internal wc_preclass_classify_ip_with_row() (public wc_preclass_classify_ip keeps its exact signature and semantics); the client_flow decision chain computes one shared wc_preclass_result_t per query and passes it to the first-hop, Phase C early-converge, Step47 early-unknown and P1 controlled-unknown candidates, while a 16-slot round-robin query-keyed cache (FNV-1a probe) inside wc_preclass_classify_query() makes repeated identical queries skip the generated-table lookup while their entry stays cached (entries are evicted round-robin, so an evicted query may be re-scanned later; observable through wc_preclass_get_lookup_count(), which the selftest uses to prove the second classification of the same query performs no new table scan). Plain-IP-only classification semantics are preserved for CIDR-listed Step47/P1 queries (classification is consulted only when the query classified and contains no '/'), so behavior is zero-change: Phase C/P0/P1/Step47/12x6/Golden/referral must all stay PASS. D4 adds selftest preclass-single-pass locking classify_query/classify_ip equivalence across representative addresses plus CIDR base classification, and a cache single-scan assertion proving a repeated query performs exactly one generated-table lookup.

D1.description: Eliminate the double table scan inside the preclass core: introduce the internal wc_preclass_classify_ip_with_row() that reuses an already-looked-up table row (falling back to the full lookup when no row is provided), keep the public wc_preclass_classify_ip() as a thin wrapper with unchanged semantics, and make wc_preclass_classify_query() pass the row it already found. It also adds a 16-slot round-robin query-keyed cache with an FNV-1a probe so repeated identical queries skip the generated-table lookup entirely; wc_preclass_get_lookup_count() exposes the row-text lookup count for the selftest.
